definitions.gloss: to be fed up with; to lose patience with; to be disgusted with
definitions.explanation: To completely lose one's goodwill or patience toward someone due to repeated disappointment. Implies that one has reached the end of their tolerance.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}に{愛想|あいそ}を{尽|つ}かされた。
examples.english: She got fed up with me.

examples.japanese: {何度|なんど}{約束|やくそく}を{破|やぶ}っても{変|か}わらないので、{愛想|あいそ}を{尽|つ}かした。
examples.english: He kept breaking promises and never changed, so I gave up on him.

examples.japanese: {社員|しゃいん}たちは{会社|かいしゃ}の{対応|たいおう}に{愛想|あいそ}を{尽|つ}かして、{次々|つぎつぎ}と{辞|や}めていった。
examples.english: The employees lost patience with the company's handling of things and quit one after another.

notes:
Literally 'to exhaust one's goodwill.' {愛想|あいそ} means friendliness or amiability, and {尽|つ}かす means to exhaust or use up completely. When someone {愛想|あいそ}を{尽|つ}かす, they have run out of all patience and goodwill.

GRAMMAR:
The person one is fed up with is marked by に: ～に{愛想|あいそ}を{尽|つ}かす. The passive form {愛想|あいそ}を{尽|つ}かされる ('to have someone give up on you') is very common.

VARIANTS:
- {愛想|あいそう}を{尽|つ}かす — variant pronunciation with long vowel
- {愛想|あいそ}{尽|づ}かし — the noun form meaning 'being fed up'

SIMILAR WORDS:
- うんざりする — to be fed up, sick of; more casual, can apply to situations as well as people
- {見限|みかぎ}る — to give up on someone; implies abandoning someone as hopeless
- {呆|あき}れる — to be exasperated; focuses on shock/disbelief at someone's behavior
